FLUX BACKUP — RECOVERY GUIDE (rsync compatibility mode)
==============================================================

These are backups of “rsync”, made by Flux Backup in rsync compatibility mode.
Every snapshot is a plain folder written by rsync, a standard Linux copying tool.
You don't need Flux to get your files back or to keep making backups.

  Profile:   rsync (rsync)
  Computer:  fixture-host, user root
  Stored in: /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync
  Written by Flux Backup 0.3.0 with rsync 3.5.2-ga8306e06
  Backed up:
  /srv/src

Never used rsync or a terminal? Read IN SHORT and NEW TO RSYNC, then use the
commands below as they are. Know rsync well? Skip to FOR RSYNC USERS at the end.

IN SHORT
--------
  Your files are ordinary files and folders. To get one back, open
    /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/latest/data
  in your file manager, go to the file's usual place (for example
  /srv/src/path/to), and copy it out. That's all: no program, no password.
  The commands below do the same from a terminal, for many files at once.

NEW TO RSYNC
------------
  rsync copies files and folders. Check that it's installed by typing
  rsync --version in a terminal; if it isn't, install the “rsync” package
  (sudo apt install rsync, sudo dnf install rsync, sudo pacman -S rsync).

  Each command below is one line: copy the whole line into a terminal and press
  Enter. Three things are worth knowing:
    * A slash at the end of a folder (folder/) means “what's inside this folder”.
      The commands below already have the slashes they need.
    * -aHAX keeps everything about the files: permissions, dates, links and
      attributes.
    * --dry-run only shows what would happen. Add it first when you're unsure.

WHERE YOUR FILES ARE
--------------------
  snapshots/<date and time>/data/<the file's usual path>
  for example
    snapshots/2026-11-09_10-31-35/data/srv/src/path/to/file

  latest points to the newest snapshot. Every snapshot is complete on its own.
  Files that didn't change are shared with the snapshot before (hard links), so
  they take space only once, and deleting one snapshot never damages another.

LIST THE SNAPSHOTS
------------------
  ls -1 /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/snapshots

BROWSE
------
  Open /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/latest/data in any file manager.

RESTORE ONE FILE
----------------
  rsync -aHAX /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/latest/data/srv/src/path/to/file /srv/src/path/to/

RESTORE A FOLDER (to where it was)
----------------------------------
  rsync -aHAX --numeric-ids /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/latest/data/srv/src/ /srv/src/

  rsync replaces files that differ. To keep your current versions too, add
  --backup --suffix=.before-restore (they're renamed instead of replaced).
  rsync never deletes files that aren't in the backup unless you add --delete.

RESTORE EVERYTHING (every backed-up path to where it was)
--------------------------------------------------------
  Look first with --dry-run, then run it for real:
  rsync -aHAX --numeric-ids --dry-run /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/latest/data/ /
  rsync -aHAX --numeric-ids /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/latest/data/ /
  Put sudo in front to restore other users' files and file owners.

RESTORE AN OLDER VERSION, OR INTO ANOTHER FOLDER
------------------------------------------------
  Use snapshots/<date and time> instead of latest, and any destination:
  rsync -aHAX /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/snapshots/2026-11-09_10-31-35/data/srv/src ~/restored/

MAKE A NEW BACKUP WITHOUT FLUX
------------------------------
  sh /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/flux-backup.sh            (or add --dry-run to only show what would change)
  It needs nothing but rsync. It does what Flux does: unchanged files are
  shared with the newest snapshot, an interrupted backup continues next
  time, and the new snapshot is named after the date and time.

WHAT IS LEFT OUT
----------------
  Exclusions from the profile:
  (none)
  Folders containing CACHEDIR.TAG are left out (their contents; the folder stays).
  rsync can't do this by itself, so Flux (and the script, with find) looks for
  them first and adds them to the rules.

DELETE OLD SNAPSHOTS
--------------------
  chmod -R u+w /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/snapshots/2025-01-31_18-00-00 && rm -rf /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/snapshots/2025-01-31_18-00-00
  (Snapshot folders can be read-only; chmod makes them deletable.) If you delete
  the newest snapshot, latest points nowhere until the next backup.

THE FILES HERE
--------------
  FLUX-RECOVERY.txt   this guide (Flux rewrites it after every backup)
  flux-backup.sh       the backup, with rsync only
  flux-repo.toml       marks this folder as Flux's
  snapshots/           the backups; latest points to the newest
  In each snapshot: data/ (your files), rsync-command.txt (the exact command that
  wrote it), rsync-filter.txt (the exclusion rules it used) and meta.json (Flux's
  notes: statistics, names, pins; never needed to restore).

FOR RSYNC USERS
---------------
  Each backup is one rsync run into snapshots/.partial, renamed to the date and time
  (local time, %Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S, _2, _3 within one second) when rsync exits 0, 23
  or 24, after which latest is repointed. An interrupted run leaves .partial in place
  and the next run continues into it. The command (Flux adds --info=progress2 --stats
  --no-human-readable to follow it):

  rsync --archive --hard-links --numeric-ids --relative --delete --delete-excluded --acls --xattrs --exclude-from=/srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/snapshots/.partial/rsync-filter.txt '--link-dest=../../<previous snapshot>/data' /srv/src/ /srv/tgt/flux-rsync/fixture-host/root/rsync/snapshots/.partial/data/

  * --relative with absolute sources: data/ mirrors /, so restores map 1:1.
  * rsync-filter.txt is first-match-wins. Flux translates the profile's gitignore-style
    patterns (last match wins) by reversing them; anchored patterns stay anchored
    to /, patterns with an inner slash are anchored, **/x becomes x.
  * Marker folders (CACHEDIR.TAG, exclude_if_present) are found before each run and
    written as “- /path/*” rules (the folder itself is kept).
  * Nothing else is Flux-specific: meta.json is optional, snapshots without it
    (made by the script or by hand) are listed by Flux, which adds a meta.json the
    next time it backs up. Flux restores from these folders with its own restore
    (identical files skipped, differing ones kept aside); the rsync commands above
    are the equivalent.
